# Plan — writing `plan.md` the organization's way

You are writing `projects/<PRJ>/intents/<NN-slug>/plan.md`. Below is what the organization's lifecycle says about this step, the sections the
artifact must carry, and its template. The lifecycle policy is the authority; this is a copy of it.

## What the lifecycle says — Plan

Template: `policies/reference/lifecycles/ai-sdlc/plan.md`

The plan lists the tasks (one board issue each), their order, a test plan and a documentation plan. Approving
the plan approves its task issues.

## What `plan.md` must carry

Open with the template's front matter and the Status line `**Status:** DRAFT`. You never write APPROVED: gov
writes it when a person approves the change request and it merges.

Then every one of these sections, as a `##` heading, in this order:

- Tasks
- Order
- Test plan
- Documentation plan
- Rollout

## The template — `policies/reference/lifecycles/ai-sdlc/plan.md`

````markdown
# Plan <NN>: <title>

<!-- An artifact made from this template carries a Status line under its title: DRAFT, then APPROVED (by whom, when, which change
     request) or STALE (why). `gov intent` and the lifecycle skills add DRAFT; gov writes APPROVED when a person approves the change request
     and it merges — never by hand. The template itself has no header lines (starters have none). -->

Spec: [spec.md](spec.md)

## Tasks
<!-- One task = one board issue = one change request. Approving this plan approves these task issues. -->
### T01 — <title>
- **Issue:** <created after approval> · **Repo:** <repo>
- **Acceptance:** <spec row it proves>
- **Depends on:** <task ids or "—">

## Order
<Which tasks go first and which run in parallel; the critical path.>

## Test plan
<For each task: the tests written first, and the tier each runs in.>

## Documentation plan
<For each task: the guides, references and examples that change with it.>

## Rollout
<How the change reaches users: release, flags, migration, and how to back it out.>
````
